newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NORTHWESTERN COACH BARNETT REJECTS NOTRE DAME.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NORTHWESTERN COACH BARNETT REJECTS NOTRE DAME.

text.p: Northwestern University football coach Gary Barnett pulled out of the running to succeed Lou Holtz as Notre Dame coach Thursday.

In a one-paragraph statement issued by Northwestern, Barnett cited "very personal and private reasons" for his decision. He said he was never offered the job although he was asked by Notre Dame officials if they could consider him a candidate after Holtz announced his resignation Tuesday.
Barnett was believed to be the leading candidate to replace Holtz, who will step down at the end of the season.
Barnett's Wildcats defeated Notre Dame at South Bend and won the Big Ten title last season. This season Northwestern is 9-2 and in second place.
Barnett signed a multi-year contract with Northwestern last year after leading the school to its first Rose Bowl appearance since 1949.

"I am very humbled and flattered that Notre Dame has asked me to be considered as a candidate," Barnett said. "However, for very personal and private reasons, I have informed Notre Dame officials that I wish not to be considered as a candidate."
Another likely candidate would be current Louisiana State coach Gerry DiNardo, who was a member of the 1973 Notre Dame team that won the national championship.

Former Notre Dame defensive coordinator and current Wisconsin coach Barry Alvarez is also a possible candidate. He led the Badgers to a Rose Bowl berth after the 1993 season, but Wisconsin has struggled this season.
